_comment: Beta overlay on foods.json, built by pipeline/blend/planner_pack.py from pipeline/blend/output/blended-cofid.json. Per standard: v = values in `keys` order (null = missing), r = [min, max, number of tables] where more than one table or a calculation gave the value, d = the definition used, c = caveat ids per nutrient key; s = each definition's values per table, in words. Foods not listed use foods.json unchanged.
status: beta: automated, without manual human verification
pointValue: median of the tables that publish the value under the same definition

definitions.calc:epaDha: EPA + DHA, calculated: (EPA + DHA) (g) x 1000, in mg

blend-beta.text: Blended values are built by automated steps without manual human verification. Each value names the tables, codes and published cells it came from.

borrowed-record.text: One of these records names another table we use as its main data source, so its values count once: they are shown, but not used in the median.

closest-definition.text: The US target is for total fibre (dietary plus functional fibre); food tables measure fibre by AOAC methods, which capture most of it but not all.

definition-not-checked.text: Which definition this standard's target uses isn't stated in the archived documents; the choice follows the standard's usual practice.

other-definition.text: This value uses a different definition from the one this standard's target uses, because the tables don't give that one for this food.

salt-basis-pantothenic.text: Combined on a data check. CoFID says it expresses pantothenate as calcium D-pantothenate; USDA reports pantothenic acid and doesn't say. If the two differed, CoFID's values would be about 9% higher (238.3 and 219.2 per pantothenate).

salt-basis-thiamin.text: Combined on a data check. CoFID says it expresses thiamin as thiamine chloride hydrochloride; USDA doesn't say. If the two differed, CoFID's values would be about 27% higher (molar masses 337.3 and 265.4).

salt-basis-vitaminB6.text: Combined on a data check. CoFID says it expresses vitamin B6 as pyridoxine hydrochloride; USDA doesn't say. If the two differed, CoFID's values would be about 22% higher (molar masses 205.6 and 169.2).
